The diagram shows a circle and a trapezium.

![A circle with radius 8.5 cm and an adjacent trapezium with top 20 cm, bottom 25 cm, and height h. Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/001-a-circle-with-radius-8-5-cm-and-an-adjacent-trap.png)

The height of the trapezium is $h$ cm.

The area of the circle is equal to the area of the trapezium.

Work out the value of $h$. 
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> When using $π$ in calculations it is helpful to use exact values, working in terms of $π$ throughout until the final answer is evaluated.
> 
> This ensures that the final answers is accurate.

> *Calculate the area of the circle using *$πr^{2}$

$π\times8.5^{2}=72.25π$

**[M1]**

> *Substitute known values into the formula for the area of a trapezium,*`1 half open parentheses a plus b close parentheses h`

`1 half open parentheses 20 plus 25 close parentheses h`

**[M1]**

> *Form an equation by, equating the expression for the area of the trapezium to the area of the circle, and solve to find the value of *$h$

`1 half open parentheses 20 plus 25 close parentheses h equals 72.25 pi`

> *Simplify*

`table row cell 1 half cross times 45 cross times h end cell equals cell 72.25 pi end cell row cell 22.5 h end cell equals cell 72.25 pi end cell end table`

> *Solve to find the value of *$h$

$h=\frac{72.25π}{22.5}\,h=10.088...$

**[M1]**

> *Round the value of *$h$* to 1 decimal place as stated in the question*

$h=10.1$

**[A1]**

![q1-4-5-very-hard-edexcel-gcse-maths](assets/019-q1-4-5-very-hard-edexcel-gcse-maths.png)

$ABCD$ is a square with a side length of $4x$ 
$M$ is the midpoint of $DC$.
 $N$ is the point on $AD$ where $ND=x$

$BMN$ is a right-angled triangle.

Find an expression, in terms of $x$, for the area of triangle $BMN$. Give your expression in its simplest form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Method 1:*

> *Calculate the area of the square **ABCD**.*

$4x\times4x=16x^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Calculate the area of the triangle **ABN, **using *$A=\frac{1}{2}bh$*, where *$b$* is the base of the triangle and *$h$* is its perpendicular height.*

![4-5-12](assets/020-4-5-12.png)

$A=\frac{1}{2}\times4x\times3x$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$A=6x^{2}$

> *Calculate the area of the triangle **BMC**.*

![4-5-11](assets/021-4-5-11.png)

$A=\frac{1}{2}\times4x\times2x$

> *Simplify.*

$A=4x^{2}$

> *Calculate the area of the triangle **MND**.*

![4-5-13](assets/022-4-5-13.png)

$A=\frac{1}{2}\timesx\times2x$

> *Simplify.*

$A=x^{2}$

> *Find the area of the shaded triangle **BNM** by subtracting the area of triangles **BMC **and** ABN **from the area of the square** ABCD.*

$16x^{2}-6x^{2}-4x^{2}-x^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$5x^{2}$* ***[1]**

** **

> *Method 2:*

> *Calculate the length **NM** on the right-angled triangle **NDM**, using Pythagoras' theorem, *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*.*

> *Substitute the given values into the formula.*

> `x squared plus open parentheses 2 x close parentheses squared equals N M squared`* *

> *Simplify.*

`table attributes columnalign right center left columnspacing 0px end attributes row cell x squared plus 4 x squared end cell equals cell N M squared end cell row cell 5 x squared end cell equals cell N M squared end cell end table`

> *Take the square root of both sides.*

$\sqrt{5}x=NM$

**[1]**

![4-5-9](assets/023-4-5-9.png)

> *Calculate the length **BM** on the right-angled triangle **BMC.*

> *Substitute the given values into Pythagoras' theorem.*

> `open parentheses 2 x close parentheses squared plus open parentheses 4 x close parentheses squared equals B M squared`* *

> *Simplify.*

`table attributes columnalign right center left columnspacing 0px end attributes row cell 4 x squared plus 16 x squared end cell equals cell B M squared end cell row cell 20 x squared end cell equals cell B M squared end cell end table`

> *Take the square root of both sides.*

$\sqrt{20}x=BM$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$2\sqrt{5}x=BM$

![4-5-10](assets/024-4-5-10.png)

> *Calculate the area of the triangle **BNM**, using *$A=\frac{1}{2}bh$*, where *$b$* is the base of the triangle and *$h$* is its perpendicular height.*

$A=\frac{1}{2}\times2\sqrt{5}x\times\sqrt{5}x$

**[1]**

> *Simplify.*

$5x^{2}$* ***[1]**

![q9-4-5-easy-edexcel-gcse-maths](assets/076-q9-4-5-easy-edexcel-gcse-maths.png)

Angie is going to varnish the floor.

She needs 1 litre of varnish for 5m<sup>2</sup> of floor. 
There are 2.5 litres of varnish in each tin of varnish.

Angie has 3 tins of varnish.

Does she have enough varnish for all the floor? 
You must show all your working.
parts.solution_md:
> *Method 1:*

> *Calculate the area of the rectangle of length 10 m and width 6 m.*

**A*** = 10 x 6 = 60 m**<sup>2</sup>*

> *Calculate the area of the small rectangle at the top centre.*

**A*** = 5 x 2 = 10 m**<sup>2</sup>*

**[1]**

> *Calculate the area of the floor by subtracting the area of the smaller rectangle from the area of the larger rectangle.*

**A*** = 60 - 10 = 50 m**<sup>2</sup>*

**Complete method to find the area of the floor ****[1]**

> *Calculate the area of the floor that Angie can varnish with her three tins. *
*Multiply the number of tins of varnish by the number of litres of varnish in each tin by the area that 1 litre will cover.*

*3 x 2.5 x 5 = 37.5 m**<sup>2</sup>*

**Complete method to find the area the varnish will cover**** [1]**** Correct areas for both the floor and the area the varnish will cover**** [1]**

> *Compare the area that the varnish will cover with the area of the floor.*

*37.5 m**<sup>2</sup>** < 50 m**<sup>2</sup>*

**Angie does not have enough varnish to cover all of the floor**** [1]**

> *Method 2:*

> *Calculate the area of the rectangle of length 10 m and width 6 m.*

**A*** = 10 x 6 = 60 m**<sup>2</sup>*

> *Calculate the area of the small rectangle at the top centre.*

**A*** = 5 x 2 = 10 m**<sup>2</sup>*

**[1]**

> *Calculate the area of the floor by subtracting the area of the smaller rectangle from the area of the larger rectangle.*

**A*** = 60 - 10 = 50 m**<sup>2</sup>*

**Complete method to find the area of the floor ****[1]**

> *Calculate the number of litres required to cover the floor by dividing the area of the floor by the number of m*<sup>*2*</sup>* that each litre will cover.*

*50*$\div$*5 = 10 litres*

**Complete method to find number of litres required to cover the floor**** [1]**

> *Calculate the number of litres of varnish that Angie has by multiply the number of tins by the number of litres in each tin.*

*3 x 2.5 = 7.5 litres*

**Correct values for both the number of litres of varnish required to cover the whole floor and the number of litres of varnish in the three tins**** [1]**

> *Compare the number of litres that Angie has with the number of litres required to cover the whole floor.*

*7.5 litres < 10 litres*

**Angie does not have enough varnish to cover all of the floor**** [1]**

ABCD is a trapezium.

![q20-paper5-nov2020-ocr-gcse-maths](assets/032-q20-paper5-nov2020-ocr-gcse-maths.png)

The perimeter of the trapezium is 56 cm. 
The ratio AD : AB : DC : BC = 5 : 12 : 6 : 5.

Calculate the area of the trapezium. 
Show your working.

..................................cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> *Split 56 cm in the ratio 5 : 12 : 6 : 5 to find the length of each side of the trapezium.*

> *Add the parts of the ratio together.*

$5+12+6+5=28$

> *Divide 56 by the total number of ratio parts.*

$56\div28=2$

**[1]**

> *Multiply each part of the ratio by 2 to find the lengths of each side.*

$\mathrm{AD}=5\times2=10\mathrm{cm}\,\mathrm{AB}=12\times2=24\mathrm{cm}\,\mathrm{DC}=6\times2=12\mathrm{cm}\,\mathrm{BC}=5\times2=10\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *The area of a trapezium can be found using the formula *`A equals 1 half open parentheses a space plus space b close parentheses h`*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the parallel sides and *$h$* is the **perpendicular **height.  *
*The perpendicular height is not known, but can be found using Pythagoras' theorem. The trapezium is an isosceles trapezium so the property that there is a line of symmetry down the middle can be used.*

![_Fylc3vx_ocr-gcse-tq-ma-are-and-perimeter-vh-q4-diagram-1](assets/033-fylc3vx-ocr-gcse-tq-ma-are-and-perimeter-vh-q4-d.png)

> *Find the distance from the point **X **(the base of the perpendicular height) to the point B.*

$XB=\frac{24-12}{2}=6\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *Use Pythagoras' theorem *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$* with the sides XB, CX and BC to find the perpendicular height of the trapezium.*

`table row cell h to the power of 2 space end exponent plus space X straight B squared space end cell equals cell space BC squared end cell row cell h to the power of 2 space end exponent plus space 6 squared space end cell equals cell space 10 squared end cell end table`

**[1]**

> *Rearrange and solve to find **h.*

`table row cell h to the power of 2 space end exponent end cell equals cell space 10 squared space minus space 6 squared end cell row blank equals cell space 100 space minus space 36 end cell row blank equals cell space 64 end cell row cell h space end cell equals cell space square root of 64 end cell row blank equals cell space 8 space cm end cell end table`

**[1]**

> *Substitute into the formula for the area of a trapezium,  *`A equals 1 half open parentheses a space plus space b close parentheses h`*, where *$a=\mathrm{AB}=24\mathrm{cm}$*, *$b=\mathrm{CD}=12\mathrm{cm}$*and *$h=8\mathrm{cm}$*.*

`A space equals space 1 half open parentheses 24 space plus space 12 close parentheses cross times 8`

**[1]**

**Area = 144 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** ****[1] **

parts.problem_md:
Here is the floor plan of a rectangular room.

![q7-paper5-june2018-ocr-gcse-maths](assets/014-q7-paper5-june2018-ocr-gcse-maths.png)

Tim buys carpet tiles for this room.

Each tile is a square measuring 50cm by 50cm.
 The tiles are only sold in packs of ten. 
Each pack costs £20.
 Tim pays for fitting at a rate of £7.50 per square metre, with any fraction of a square metre rounded up.

Work out the **total** cost of the tiles and fitting.

£ ..........................
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert everything into the same units, either m or cm. Working in cm will usually be easier. *

*Width: 3 m = 300 cm *
*Length: 4.5 m = 450 cm*

> *To find the number of carpet tiles needed, first check that the tiles fit exactly into the room by checking that both the width and the length divide exactly by 50 cm. Find the number of tiles that go along the width of the room.*

*Width: 300 ÷ 50 = 6 tiles*

**[1]**

> *Find the number of tiles that go along the length of the room.*

*Length: 450 ÷ 50 = 9 tiles*

**[1]**

> *So to fit the tiles perfectly into the room there will be 9 tiles by 6 tiles.  Find the total number of tiles needed.*

*Width × Length = 6 × 9 tiles *
*Total = 54 tiles.*

**[1]**

> *Tiles are sold in packs of ten, so the total number of packs needed will be 6 packs.  Find the cost of 6 packs, at £20 per pack.*

*Total cost of 6 packs at £20 per pack = 6 × £20 = £120*

**[1]**

> *To find the cost of fitting, calculate the area of the room by multiplying the length (4.5 m) by the width (3 m). The cost is given per square metre here so it is easier to work in metres.*

$A_{\mathrm{room}}=4.5\times3=13.5m^{2}$

> *Round this up to the nearest square metre before finding the cost, as any fraction of a square metre is rounded up.*

*13.5 m**<sup>2 </sup>** = 14 m**<sup>2 </sup>**(next m**<sup>2</sup>**)*

> *The fitting costs £7.50 per square metre, so multiply this by the number of s quare metres in the room. *

*14 × £7.50 = £105.00*

**[1]**

> *Add this to the cost of the carpet tiles.*

*£105.00 + £120.00*

> *Write money in pounds to 2 decimal places.*

**£225.00 ****[1] **

![q11-paper-1h-june-2018-aqa-gcse-maths](assets/059-q11-paper-1h-june-2018-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

The perimeter of one small rectangle is 15 cm

Work out the perimeter of the large rectangle.

.............................cm
parts.solution_md:
> *Notice that the width of the rectangle is half of its length. *

*Let the width of the rectangle be *$x$*, then the length of the rectangle is *$2x$*.*

**[1]**

> *Add these dimensions to a small rectangle on the diagram.*

![gcse-aqa-tq-area-and-perimeter-h-q15](assets/060-gcse-aqa-tq-area-and-perimeter-h-q15.png)

> *Form an equation by adding the four edges of the small rectangle together and letting it equal 15.*

$2x+x+2x+x=15$

**[1]**

> *Simplify and solve to find *$x$*.*

`table row cell 6 x space end cell equals cell space 15 end cell row cell x space end cell equals cell space 15 over 6 space equals space 2.5 space cm end cell end table`

**[1]**

> *So the width of a small rectangle is 2.5 cm and the length is 5 cm.*

> *Add these to the outside of the diagram.*

![gcse-aqa-tq-area-and-perimeter-h-q15-diagram-2](assets/061-gcse-aqa-tq-area-and-perimeter-h-q15-diagram-2.png)

> *Find the perimeter by adding the lengths around edge of the big rectangle together.*

$P=5+2.5+5+2.5+5+2.5+2.5$

** ****Perimeter = 25 cm**** [1]**

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows equilateral triangle $ABC$ with sides of length 10 cm.
A circle is drawn inside the triangle.

![Triangle with inscribed circle, labelled ABC, points DEF on edges. An arrow marks 10 cm from A to B. Note: Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/003-triangle-with-inscribed-circle-labelled-abc-poin.png)

$D,E$ and $F$ are points on the circle

$ADB,BEC$ and $CFA$ are tangents to the circle.

Calculate the total area of the regions shown shaded in the diagram. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solution_md:
> *First find the area of the whole triangle*

> **[exam-tip]**
> Remember the area for any triangle can be found using the formula $\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$. It is an equilateral triangle, so the angles are all equal to 60°.

`table row cell 1 half space cross times space 10 space cross times space 10 space cross times space sin open parentheses 60 close parentheses space end cell equals cell space 25 square root of 3 end cell row blank equals cell 43.30... cm squared end cell end table`

**[M1]**

> *Create a right-angled triangle to find the radius of the circle*

![Triangle ABC with inscribed circle. Angle A is 30 degrees, AD is 5 cm, DB is 10 cm. Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/004-triangle-abc-with-inscribed-circle-angle-a-is-30.png)

> *Use SOHCAHTOA to find *$r$

`tan open parentheses 30 close parentheses space equals fraction numerator space r over denominator 5 end fraction`

`5 space cross times space tan open parentheses 30 close parentheses space equals space r`

$r=\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{3}$

**[M1]**

> *Find the area of the circle*

`table row cell straight pi space cross times space open parentheses fraction numerator 5 square root of 3 over denominator 3 end fraction close parentheses squared space end cell equals cell fraction numerator space 25 over denominator 3 end fraction straight pi end cell row blank equals cell 26.17... space cm squared end cell end table`

**[A1]**

> *Subtract the area of the circle from the area of the triangle to find the shaded area*

$25\sqrt{3}-\frac{25}{3}π=17.121...$

> *Round to 3 significant figures*

$17.1\mathrm{cm}^{2}$

**[A1]**
